mainTopic: The כהן גדול's וידוי, the lottery משנה with its list of praised donors, and the גמרא on the מזבח's position, walking beside a teacher, the lots, and בן קטין's כיור
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא that uses the word 'כַּפָּרָה' to show two things about the כהן גדול's וידוי: it opens with 'אָנָּא', learned from משה at חורב, and it includes God's שם, learned from עגלה ערופה. אביי asks why עגלה ערופה does not also take 'אָנָּא' from חורב, and the גמרא leaves this as a קשיא. Two פסוקים are then brought as sources for the people answering when the שם is said. A new משנה describes where the כהן גדול stands for the lottery over the two goats. It then lists people praised for improving the מקדש: בן גמלא, בן קטין, מונבז, הילני and ניקנור. In the גמרא, the words 'north of the מזבח' are matched to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and the earlier משנה is re-read so that it fits his view too. The גמרא then works out exactly where a student walks beside his teacher. It also explains the rules of the lots: one for each goat, identical, and made of any material. Next it explains בן קטין's spouts and wheel. It ends by asking why מונבז made only gold handles and not whole gold vessels; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Source for saying 'Please' in the confession
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns that the וִידּוּי opens with 'אָנָּא' through a גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה on 'כַּפָּרָה' with משה's prayer at חוֹרֵב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know the confession uses 'please'? 'Atonement' is said here, and 'atonement' is said at חוֹרֵב. Just as there it says 'please', so too here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for why the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל begins his וִידּוּי with 'אָנָּא'. It answers with a word-link to the חֵטְא הָעֵגֶל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כַּפָּרָה' shows up in the יוֹם כִּפּוּר פְּסוּקִים and also when משה said 'אוּלַי אֲכַפְּרָה' after the עֵגֶל. Right after that, משה prayed 'אָנָּא, חָטָא הָעָם הַזֶּה'. Because the two places share the same word, the way משה confessed becomes the model for the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we know)? It asks for a source.
Please; the opening word of the וִידּוּי
Atonement; the word that links the two places
Horeb (Sinai), where משה prayed after the עֵגֶל
Just as there, so too here; the formula of a גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is with 'please'?
It says here 'atonement',
and it says there, at Horeb, 'atonement'.
Just as there it is with 'please',
so too here it is with 'please'.

steps.raayaObject: That the וִידּוּי of the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל opens with 'אָנָּא'
steps.raayaSupportSource: גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה of 'כַּפָּרָה' with משה's prayer at חוֹרֵב (שמות לב)

steps.title: Source for saying God's Name in the confession
steps.stepSummary: Through the same word 'כַּפָּרָה', the ברייתא learns from עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה that the וִידּוּי includes the שֵׁם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know it uses the Name? 'Atonement' is said here, and 'atonement' is said by the heifer whose neck is broken. Just as there the Name is used, so too here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second word-link. This one shows that the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל says God's שֵׁם in his וִידּוּי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה the כֹּהֲנִים say 'כַּפֵּר לְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל', and that פָּסוּק contains God's שֵׁם. The shared word 'כַּפָּרָה' carries that detail over to יוֹם כִּפּוּר. So the וִידּוּי gets one feature from חוֹרֵב ('אָנָּא') and a different feature from עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה (the שֵׁם).

keyTerms.meaning: The heifer whose neck is broken, brought for an unsolved murder (דברים כא)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is with 'the Name'?
It says here 'atonement',
and it says by the heifer whose neck is broken 'atonement'.
Just as there it is with the Name,
so too here it is with the Name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second derivation using the same method, from a different source
steps.raayaObject: That the וִידּוּי includes God's שֵׁם
steps.raayaSupportSource: גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה of 'כַּפָּרָה' with עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה (דברים כא:ח)

steps.title: אביי asks why עגלה ערופה doesn't learn from חורב
steps.stepSummary: אַבָּיֵי grants that חוֹרֵב cannot learn from עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה, because it already happened. But he asks why עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה should not learn 'אָנָּא' from חוֹרֵב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It makes sense that חורב doesn't learn from עגלה ערופה, because what happened, happened. But עגלה ערופה should learn from חורב!
steps.whatsHappening: אַבָּיֵי starts a challenge that uses the same word-link but runs it in the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's prayer at חוֹרֵב came before the מִצְוָה of עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה was given. So it makes sense that חוֹרֵב does not pick up the שֵׁם from עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה. But עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה came later, so it could learn from חוֹרֵב and should also say 'אָנָּא'.

keyTerms.meaning: What was, was; a past event cannot be changed

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא חוֹרֵב מֵעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה לָא יָלֵיף —
phrases.english: Granted, Horeb does not learn from the heifer whose neck is broken,
because what was, was.
But let the heifer whose neck is broken learn from Horeb!

steps.kashyaTarget: The two-way logic of the גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'כַּפָּרָה' links the places, the later case (עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה) should pick up 'אָנָּא' from the earlier case (חוֹרֵב).

steps.title: The משנה shows the heifer declaration has no 'Please'
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer that עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה really does say 'אָנָּא'. A משנה blocks that answer, because it quotes the כֹּהֲנִים without 'אָנָּא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that is indeed so, but we learned: 'The priests say: Atone for Your nation Israel', and they do not say 'please'.
steps.whatsHappening: אַבָּיֵי closes off a possible way out. A משנה shows that the עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה declaration has no 'אָנָּא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The way out would be to say 'yes, they also say אָנָּא'. But the משנה in סוטה gives the exact words the כֹּהֲנִים say, and 'אָנָּא' is missing. So the question gets stronger: why doesn't the גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה work in this direction?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; brings up a possible answer
But we learned in a משנה!

phrases.english: And if you say that is indeed so,
but we learned in a mishna:
'The priests say: Atone for Your nation Israel',
whereas it does not say 'please'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible answer to אביי's question
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה also uses 'אָנָּא'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה quotes the exact words, and 'אָנָּא' is not there.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that אַבָּיֵי's question is a real difficulty and gives no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion by saying the question has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קַשְׁיָא' means the problem is real but the גמרא leaves it open. The two sources for the וִידּוּי still stand. What is left unexplained is why עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה does not take 'אָנָּא' from חוֹרֵב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a question left without an answer

steps.confusionAlert: 'קַשְׁיָא' is not 'תְּיוּבְתָּא'. It does not throw out the ברייתא's sources. It only marks one question as unanswered.
steps.whatToRemember: The וִידּוּי gets 'אָנָּא' from חוֹרֵב and the שֵׁם from עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה. Why the link does not run back from חוֹרֵב to עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה stays a קַשְׁיָא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אַבָּיֵי's question stands without an answer.

steps.title: רבי's source for answering when God's Name is said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'וְהֵן עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו'. Then רַבִּי brings a source from משה's words in הַאֲזִינוּ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they answer after him. It was taught: רבי says: 'When I call the name of God, give glory to our God.' משה told ישראל: When I mention the Name of the הקדוש ברוך הוא, you give glory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the משנה, that the people answer after the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, and brings a ברייתא with a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פָּסוּק in הַאֲזִינוּ connects 'calling God's שֵׁם' with 'giving glory'. רַבִּי reads it as משה telling the people what to do: when he says the שֵׁם, they should respond with praise. That is why the people respond to the שֵׁם in the וִידּוּי.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for answering 'בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ' or 'אָמֵן' when the שֵׁם is mentioned.

phrases.english: And they respond after him.
It was taught: Rebbi says:
'When I call the name of the Lord,'
'give glory to our God',
Moses said to Israel:
When I mention
the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
you give glory.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵן עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו. תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר
steps.raayaObject: That the people respond when the שֵׁם is mentioned
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים לב:ג, 'כִּי שֵׁם ה׳ אֶקְרָא הָבוּ גוֹדֶל לֵאלֹהֵינוּ'

steps.title: חנניה's alternate source from משלי
steps.stepSummary: חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ brings a different source for the same practice, 'זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנניה, the son of רבי יהושע's brother, says: 'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing.' The prophet told ישראל: When I mention the Righteous One of the worlds, you give a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תַּנָּא gives another פָּסוּק that teaches the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חֲנַנְיָה reads 'צַדִּיק' as God, the צַדִּיק of all worlds. In his reading, שְׁלֹמֹה is telling the people to bless God whenever He is mentioned. The rule is the same as רַבִּי's, and only the source is different.

keyTerms.meaning: The memory of the righteous is for a blessing (משלי י:ז)
Righteous One of the worlds, meaning God

phrases.aramaic: חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Chananya, son of the brother of Rabbi Yehoshua, says:
'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing',
the prophet said to Israel:
When I mention the Righteous One of the worlds,
you give a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different source for the same rule
steps.raayaObject: That the people respond when God is mentioned
steps.whatToRemember: Two sources for answering when the שֵׁם is said: רַבִּי uses 'הָבוּ גוֹדֶל' (הַאֲזִינוּ), and חֲנַנְיָה uses 'זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה' (משלי).

steps.title: New משנה: where the High Priest stands for the lottery
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל goes to the eastern part of the עֲזָרָה, north of the מִזְבֵּחַ, with the סְגָן on his right and the רֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב on his left.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to the east of the courtyard, to the north of the altar. The deputy was on his right and the head of the family on his left.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes where the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל stands to get ready for the lottery over the goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל moves to the north side, where the קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים are slaughtered. He stands between two officials. The סְגָן, the most senior assistant, stands on the more important right side.

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the family group of כֹּהֲנִים serving that day

phrases.english: MISHNA:
He came to the east of the courtyard,
to the north of the altar,
the deputy at his right
and the head of the family at his left.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל stands east of the עֲזָרָה, north of the מִזְבֵּחַ, between the סְגָן (right) and the רֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב (left).

steps.title: The two goats, the box, and the golden lots
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the two שְׂעִירִים, the קַלְפִּי with two lots, and how בֶּן גַּמְלָא replaced the boxwood lots with gold ones and was praised for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there were two goats there, and a box was there with two lots in it. They were of boxwood, and בן גמלא made them of gold, and they would mention him for praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues setting up the lottery. It lists the goats and the lots, and it records the improvement בֶּן גַּמְלָא made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lots decide which goat is 'לַה׳' and which is 'לַעֲזָאזֵל'. They were first made of plain boxwood. בֶּן גַּמְלָא, a כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, made them of gold, and the משנה records that he was remembered with praise.

phrases.english: And there were two goats there,
and a lottery box was there,
and in it two lots;
they were of boxwood,
and Ben Gamla made them of gold,
and they would mention him favorably.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two goats and a box with two lots. The lots were first boxwood, and בֶּן גַּמְלָא made them gold and was praised.
steps.whatToRemember: The lottery setting: the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל stands north of the מִזְבֵּחַ, the two goats are there, and the lots are in a קַלְפִּי. The lots were made gold by בֶּן גַּמְלָא, who was remembered with praise.

steps.title: בן קטין improves the washing basin
steps.stepSummary: The משנה praises בן קטין for adding spouts to the כיור and making a machine that kept its water from becoming פסול overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן קטין made twelve spouts for the כיור, because before that it had only two. He also made a machine for the כיור, so that its water would not become פסול by staying overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of people who improved the בית המקדש. This time it praises בן קטין for two upgrades to the כיור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only two spouts, only two כהנים could wash their hands and feet at the same time. Twelve spouts let many כהנים wash at once. The machine lowered the כיור into flowing water at night, so the water was not 'left overnight' and stayed usable the next morning.

keyTerms.meaning: The copper basin the כהנים used to wash their hands and feet
A machine (a lifting wheel) used to lower the basin
Become unfit by being left overnight

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן קָטִין עָשָׂה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר דַּד לַכִּיּוֹר,
phrases.english: Ben Katin made twelve spouts for the basin,
because it had only two.
phrases.notes: More spouts meant more כהנים could wash at the same time.

phrases.english: He also made a machine for the basin,
so that its water would not become unfit by staying overnight.
phrases.notes: The basin was sunk into flowing water at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן קָטִין עָשָׂה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר דַּד לַכִּיּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of praised donors that started with בן גמלא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן קטין is remembered with praise for adding twelve spouts and a machine to the כיור.

steps.title: מונבז המלך and הילני המלכה give gold items
steps.stepSummary: מונבז המלך paid for gold handles on the יום הכיפורים vessels. His mother הילני gave a gold chandelier and a gold tablet with פרשת סוטה written on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: King מונבז would make all the handles of the יום הכיפורים vessels out of gold. His mother הילני made a gold chandelier over the entrance of the היכל. She also made a gold tablet with פרשת סוטה written on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing donors. Here it names a king and his mother, the queen, and the gold items they gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gold handles made the יום הכיפורים vessels more beautiful. The gold tablet had a practical use: when a סוטה was tested, the כהן could copy her פרשה from the tablet instead of taking out a ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah section about a wife suspected of being unfaithful (במדבר ה)

phrases.english: King Munbaz would make

phrases.aramaic: כָּל יְדוֹת הַכֵּלִים שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.english: all the handles of the Yom Kippur vessels of gold.

phrases.aramaic: הֵילֶנִי אִמּוֹ עָשְׂתָה נִבְרֶשֶׁת שֶׁל זָהָב
phrases.english: Helene his mother made a gold chandelier
over the entrance of the Sanctuary,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף הִיא עָשְׂתָה טַבְלָא שֶׁל זָהָב
phrases.english: and she also made a gold tablet
on which the section of the sotah was written.
phrases.notes: Used for copying the פרשה for the סוטה process.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹנְבַּז הַמֶּלֶךְ הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה כָּל יְדוֹת הַכֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more names to the משנה's list of donors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מונבז and הילני are praised for their gold gifts to the בית המקדש.

steps.title: ניקנור's doors and the praise for all the donors
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions the miracles that happened to ניקנור's doors and ends by saying all these people were remembered with praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Miracles were done for ניקנור's doors. And people would mention all of them with praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with ניקנור. Then it closes the whole list by saying all these donors were remembered for good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the others, ניקנור is praised because of miracles done for the doors he brought, not for a new object he designed. The closing line 'והיו מזכירין אותן לשבח' covers everyone in the list, in contrast to the people the next משנה mentions for disgrace.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who brought the doors for the eastern gate of the עזרה, later named for him
For praise; in a good way

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists people who improved the בית המקדש (בן גמלא, בן קטין, מונבז, הילני, ניקנור), and all of them were remembered with praise.

phrases.english: For Nicanor, miracles were done for his doors,
and they would mention them with praise.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means all the donors in the list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of donors and sums it up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the listed donors, including ניקנור, were remembered with praise.

steps.title: The גמרא learns that the altar was not in the north
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. It looks at the words 'to the north of the מזבח' and learns that the מזבח itself must not stand in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Since the משנה says 'to the north of the מזבח,' we can learn from this that the מזבח itself does not stand in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words from Step 8, where the כהן גדול goes 'to the north of the מזבח.' It draws an inference from that wording. This sets up the next question: whose opinion is this?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מזבח were in the north part of the עזרה, saying 'north of the מזבח' would not mark off a separate northern area. The wording suggests that the north is one area and the מזבח is outside it, in the south.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; we learn from this
North; the northern area of the עזרה where קדשי קדשים are slaughtered

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Since it says 'to the north of the altar,'
we learn that the altar does not stand in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא now analyzes the wording of the משנה in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה's wording, the מזבח was not located in the north.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the מזבח was not in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known debate among the תנאים about whether the מזבח stood partly in the north or fully in the south. Since the משנה implies it was not in the north, the גמרא wants to match it to the right side of that debate.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the inference: now we need to know who holds it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the מזבח does not stand in the north?

steps.title: It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the whole north stays empty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He learns from 'צפונה לפני ה׳' that the whole north must be left empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. As a ברייתא teaches: 'צפונה לפני ה׳' means that the whole north must be empty. These are the words of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question and brings a ברייתא as proof. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds the northern area must be fully clear, so the מזבח was entirely in the south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the קרבן is slaughtered 'on the side of the מזבח, northward.' רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads this to mean the whole northern area must be free of the מזבח. That matches the משנה's wording 'north of the מזבח.'

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.
As it was taught: 'Northward before God,'
that the entire north must be empty,
phrases.notes: So the מזבח is entirely in the south.

phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says the whole north is empty and the מזבח is entirely in the south.

steps.title: But the earlier part followed אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the earlier משנה was already explained as following אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds a different view. Can the two parts follow two different Tannaim?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first part (the earlier משנה) follows אלעזר ברבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the answer it just gave. Earlier, it explained the previous משנה according to אלעזר ברבי שמעון, so now the משנה seems to switch opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said the כהן גדול's פר stood between the אולם and the מזבח. The גמרא had explained that this follows אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who counts that area as 'north,' meaning the מזבח reaches partly into the north. That clashes with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says the whole north is empty.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part; the earlier clause
A Tanna who holds the מזבח stood partly in the north

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the names: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (whole north empty) and אלעזר ברבי שמעון (the area between the אולם and the מזבח counts as north). They hold opposite views here.

phrases.english: But the first clause
is Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רֵישָׁא אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier part of the same משנה was explained as following אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who disagrees. It is unlikely that one משנה switches between opposing opinions.

steps.title: The whole משנה is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב; read the earlier part differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the entire משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The earlier line should be read as 'next to the area between the אולם and the מזבח.'
steps.simpleTranslation: All of it is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Teach the earlier line as 'next to the area between the אולם and the מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by putting the whole משנה under רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. It changes the reading of the earlier משנה slightly so it fits his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, we thought the פר stood exactly between the אולם and the מזבח, which only works for אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Now the line is read as 'next to' that area, off to the side in the real north. That place counts as north for everyone. So no part of the משנה needs אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it; the whole משנה
And teach (read the text this way)
The entrance hall in front of the היכל

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה implies the מזבח was not in the north, so it follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. To keep the whole משנה consistent, the גמרא reads the earlier line as 'next to the area between the אולם and the מזבח.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: rather than split one משנה between two opposing תנאים, it adjusts the reading of one line so the whole משנה follows one opinion.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא,
phrases.english: All of it is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
and teach: 'next to between the Entrance Hall and the altar.'
phrases.notes: Meaning beside that area, in the true north, not directly between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא, וּתְנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the text of the earlier משנה (ותני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier line means the פר stood directly between the אולם and the מזבח, which only fits אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line means 'next to' that area, in the real north, so the whole משנה fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: deputy on the right, family head on the left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the סגן stood to the right of the כהן גדול and the ראש בית אב to his left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The deputy is at his right, and the head of the family group is at his left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the next discussion about where a student should walk relative to his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the כהן גדול went to draw the lots, two people walked beside him. The סגן, who is second in rank, was on his right. The ראש בית אב, the head of that day's priestly family, was on his left.

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy כהן גדול, second in rank
Head of the priestly family group serving that day

phrases.english: The deputy is at his right,
and the head of the patrilineal family is at his left.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַסְּגָן בִּימִינוֹ, וְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה after finishing the discussion about the north side and the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סגן walks on the כהן גדול's right and the ראש בית אב on his left.

steps.title: Walking on your teacher's right is boorish
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a person who walks on the right side of his teacher is a בור, someone with no manners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Someone who walks on the right side of his teacher is a boor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה states a rule of good manners. A student should not walk on his teacher's right side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right side is the place of honor. Walking there makes the student look equal to his teacher, or even more important. That is why רב יהודה calls such a student a בור.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
One who walks to the right of his teacher
is a boor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings in a rule of manners that seems to clash with the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student must not walk on his teacher's right side.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: the deputy walks on the right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה. In our משנה, the סגן, who is like a student, walks on the כהן גדול's right.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: The deputy is at his right, and the head of the family group is at his left!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's rule using the משנה it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סגן ranks below the כהן גדול, so he is like a student next to his teacher. Yet the משנה places him on the right. This seems to go directly against רב יהודה's rule.

phrases.english: We learned: The deputy is at his right,
and the head of the patrilineal family is at his left!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that walking on the teacher's right is boorish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה puts the lower-ranked סגן on the right side of the higher-ranked כהן גדול.

steps.title: A second challenge from a ברייתא and from the three angels
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when three walk together, the teacher is in the middle, the greater student on his right and the lesser on his left. The same order is found with the three angels who visited אברהם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, a ברייתא teaches: When three people walk on the road, the teacher goes in the middle, the greater student on his right, and the lesser on his left. We find the same with the three ministering angels who came to אברהם: מיכאל was in the middle, גבריאל on his right, and רפאל on his left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge against רב יהודה from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the right side to the more important student. That means students are supposed to walk on the teacher's right. The angels show the same order, with מיכאל, the greatest, in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught in a baraita:
Three who were walking on the road —
the teacher is in the middle,
the greater on his right, and the lesser on his left.
And so we find with the three ministering angels
who came to Abraham:
Michael in the middle,
Gabriel on his right, and Raphael on his left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge against רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives the right side, the place of honor, to the leading student. So a student is expected to walk on his teacher's right.

steps.title: The student walks slightly behind, partly covered by his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר פפא explains that the sources describe a student on the right who walks slightly back, so his teacher partly covers him. רב יהודה only objects to walking right beside the teacher as an equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר פפא explained it before רב אדא: He walks in a way that his teacher partly covers him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges. Being on the right is fine, as long as the student stays a little behind his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's problem is a student who walks level with his teacher on the right. When the student hangs slightly back, the teacher clearly leads and partly hides him. So the משנה and the ברייתא do not contradict רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: That he be covered or hidden

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Pappa explained it
before Rav Adda:
so that he is covered by his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges in steps 20 and 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: separating walking level with the teacher from walking slightly behind
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources seemed to allow walking right beside the teacher on his right.
steps.terutzMaskana: The student may be on the right, but slightly back, so his teacher partly covers him.

steps.title: But walking behind your teacher is arrogant
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that walking level with your teacher is boorish, and walking behind him is arrogant. This seems to rule out רב שמואל בר פפא's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: Someone who walks right next to his teacher is a boor. Someone who walks behind his teacher is one of the arrogant!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given, using another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking behind the teacher looks like it is not allowed either. The ברייתא itself does not explain why walking behind counts as arrogant. So 'slightly behind' seems to run into this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַמְהַלֵּךְ כְּנֶגֶד רַבּוֹ — הֲרֵי זֶה בּוּר,
phrases.english: One who walks beside his teacher is a boor;

phrases.aramaic: אֲחוֹרֵי רַבּוֹ — הֲרֵי זֶה מִגַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ!
phrases.english: behind his teacher, he is among the arrogant!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב שמואל בר פפא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the student walks slightly behind his teacher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Walking behind the teacher is called arrogant, so the answer seems to describe a forbidden way of walking.

steps.title: He walks off to the side, only slightly back
steps.stepSummary: The student is neither fully beside his teacher nor fully behind him. He walks off to the side and slightly back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He walks off a little to the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and closes the topic. The correct position is in between: to the side and a bit back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being fully level is boorish, and being fully behind is arrogant. A diagonal position, off to the side and a little back, avoids both problems. This fits the משנה, both ברייתות, and רב יהודה together.

keyTerms.meaning: Walks off to the side, at an angle

steps.whatToRemember: A student walks on his teacher's right, but off to the side and slightly behind him. He should not walk level with him or directly behind him.

phrases.english: He walks off slightly to the side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a middle position between 'level with' and 'behind'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Slightly behind' seemed to be the same as the forbidden 'behind'.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is not directly behind his teacher, only off to the side at a slight angle.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the lottery box with two lots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: there was a קלפי there, and in it were two lots.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was a lottery box there, and in it were two lots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. This sets up a ברייתא about what the lots may be made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור, the כהן גדול drew two lots from this box. The lots decided which goat would be offered to ה׳ and which would be sent to עזאזל.

keyTerms.meaning: A box or urn holding the lots

phrases.english: And there was a lottery receptacle there,
and in it were two lots.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַלְפִּי הָיְתָה שָׁם וּבָהּ שְׁנֵי גוֹרָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic after the discussion about walking beside a teacher ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There was a קלפי with two lots in it.

steps.title: Lots may be made of any material
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the גורלות may be made of any material, because the תורה just says 'lots' without naming a material.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים taught: 'And אהרן shall place lots on the two goats.' This means lots of any material.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains a detail of the משנה's lots: what they can be made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the general word 'lots' and does not say what they must be made of. So the ברייתא concludes that any material works.

keyTerms.meaning: Goats (the two goats of יום כיפור)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next discussion in the גמרא about exactly which materials may be used for the lots.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And Aaron shall place lots on the two goats":
lots of any material.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a detail of the משנה line quoted in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lots may be made from any material.

steps.title: Only one lot per goat, not two
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the idea of putting two lots on each goat. The פסוק says 'one lot for ה׳ and one lot for עזאזל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he should put two lots on this goat and two lots on that goat. So the פסוק says: 'One lot for ה׳ and one lot for עזאזל.' There is only one lot here for ה׳, and only one lot here for עזאזל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and rules out a mistaken way of doing the lottery: using more than one lot per side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first raises a possible mistake with יכול ('you might think'), then corrects it with a פסוק. The word אחד ('one') in the פסוק limits it to exactly one lot for ה׳ and one for עזאזל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think.' Introduces a mistaken idea that the פסוק will correct.
'The verse teaches.' Introduces the פסוק that settles the question.
The goat sent away into the wilderness on יום כיפור.
For ה׳, meaning the goat offered as a קרבן.

phrases.english: One might think he should place two on this one
and two on that one,
therefore the verse states:
"One lot for God and one lot for Azazel"

phrases.aramaic: — אֵין כָּאן לַשֵּׁם אֶלָּא גּוֹרָל אֶחָד,
phrases.english: — there is only one lot here for God,
and there is only one here for Azazel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from Step 26 about the גורלות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each side gets exactly one lot: one for ה׳ and one for עזאזל.

steps.title: Not a full set of both lots on each goat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects a second mistaken setup: putting a ה׳ lot and an עזאזל lot on each goat. The פסוק again limits it to one of each in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he should put a ה׳ lot and an עזאזל lot on this goat, and also a ה׳ lot and an עזאזל lot on that goat. So the פסוק says 'one lot for ה׳'. There is only one for ה׳ and only one for עזאזל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rules out another wrong arrangement, where each goat would get a full pair of lots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 ruled out two identical lots per side. This step rules out doubling the whole set, which would make four lots in total. The same word אחד proves that the entire lottery uses only two lots.

keyTerms.meaning: The lot marked for ה׳ and the lot marked for עזאזל.
'One lot.' The words in the פסוק that limit the count.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יִתֵּן שֶׁל שֵׁם וְשֶׁל עֲזָאזֵל עַל זֶה
phrases.english: One might think he should place the lot of God and of Azazel on this one

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל שֵׁם וְשֶׁל עֲזָאזֵל עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: and the lot of God and of Azazel on that one,
therefore the verse states:
"One lot for God"
— there is only one here for God,
and there is only one here for Azazel.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִתֵּן שֶׁל שֵׁם וְשֶׁל עֲזָאזֵל עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second 'you might think' that the same פסוק rules out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lottery uses only two lots in total, not one full set for each goat.

steps.title: Then why does the Torah say 'lots' in the plural?
steps.stepSummary: If there is only one lot for each side, the ברייתא asks what the plural word גורלות comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'lots' (plural)?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up its next teaching. It points out that the plural word 'גורלות' now seems unnecessary, since we already know the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know there are exactly two lots, so the plural adds no information about how many. That means the extra word must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so.' Draws a consequence from what was just said.
'What does the verse come to teach?' Asks for the purpose of an extra word.

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying "lots"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion of Steps 27–28 that the number of lots is fixed at two.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the plural word גורלות teaches, now that it is not needed for the count.

steps.title: The two lots must be identical
steps.stepSummary: The plural teaches that the two lots must be the same. One cannot be gold and the other silver, and one cannot be big and the other small.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that they must be equal. He should not make one of gold and one of silver, or one big and one small.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: the plural word groups the two lots together as a matching pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling them together 'lots' treats them as one matching set. If the lots were different, the כהן גדול could tell them apart by feel, and the lottery would no longer be random.
steps.whatToRemember: There is one lot for ה׳ and one for עזאזל, and the two lots must be identical in material and size.

phrases.english: — that they should be identical,
that he should not make one of gold
and one of silver,
one big and one small.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural גורלות teaches that the two lots must match in material and size.

steps.title: Why say lots can be made of anything? That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's line 'lots of any material'. The Torah never names a material, so this seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Lots of any material.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the opening words of the ברייתא from Step 26 and objects that they teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not name a material, so any material should naturally be allowed. The challenge asks why the ברייתא bothered to state it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is obvious!' Challenges a statement as unnecessary.

phrases.english: Lots of any material:
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ruling quoted in Step 26 and questions why it needed to be said.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that lots may be made of any material.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah names no material, so it is obvious that any material works.

steps.title: Without the פסוק, we would have required gold like the ציץ
steps.stepSummary: The statement is needed. Since the ציץ has ה׳'s name and is made of gold, we might have required gold lots too. The double word 'גורל' includes other materials, such as olive wood, walnut, and boxwood.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed, because of what a ברייתא teaches. We find that the ציץ has ה׳'s name written on it and is made of gold. You might think this lot must be the same. So the פסוק says 'lot... lot', which includes other materials: it includes olive wood, it includes walnut, it includes boxwood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge. It shows a real reason we might have thought gold was required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lot for ה׳ has ה׳'s name written on it, just like the ציץ, which is made of gold. That comparison could have made gold seem required. The repeated word 'גורל' in the פסוק is read as a ריבוי (an inclusion) to allow ordinary wood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is only needed for...' Introduces the reason a statement is not obvious.
'Because of what was taught in a ברייתא.'
The gold plate on the כהן גדול's forehead, with ה׳'s name written on it.
'It included.' The פסוק widens the rule to cover more cases.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: when a rule seems obvious, the גמרא finds a reasonable comparison (here, the ציץ) that could have led to a different answer.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary, due to what was taught:
Because we find with the frontplate
that the Name is written on it
and it is of gold,
one might think this too is so —
the verse states: "lot," "lot", to include,
it includes one of olive wood,
it includes one of walnut,
it includes one of boxwood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of Step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reasonable comparison (the ציץ) that makes the statement necessary.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ה׳ lot has ה׳'s name on it like the gold ציץ, we might have required gold.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double word 'גורל' includes any material, such as olive wood, walnut, or boxwood.

steps.title: משנה: בן קטין made twelve spouts for the כיור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: בן קטין added twelve spouts to the כיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן קטין made twelve spouts for the כיור, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה and sets up a ברייתא that will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the כיור had only two spouts, as the משנה itself states ('שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ אֶלָּא שְׁנַיִם'). The משנה credits בן קטין, a כהן גדול, with adding more, and the next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול who made improvements in the בית המקדש.
The copper basin the כהנים used to wash their hands and feet.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן קָטִין עָשָׂה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר דַּד
phrases.english: Ben Katin made twelve spouts
for the basin, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן קָטִין עָשָׂה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר דַּד לַכִּיּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the lots and goes to the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן קטין added twelve spouts to the כיור.

steps.title: Why twelve: so the twelve תמיד כהנים could wash together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the twelve spouts let the twelve כהנים who bring the תמיד wash their hands and feet at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: this was so that his twelve fellow כהנים who work on the תמיד could wash their hands and feet all at once.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the reason for the number twelve in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן תמיד was handled by a team of twelve כהנים, as the גמרא explained earlier. With twelve spouts, none of them had to wait in line to wash.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily קרבן brought every morning and afternoon.
Washing hands and feet before doing the עבודה.

phrases.english: It was taught: so that
twelve of his fellow priests
who are occupied with the daily offering
could sanctify their hands and feet at once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה in Step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twelve spouts let the twelve תמיד כהנים wash at the same time.

steps.title: Upper spouts in the morning, lower spouts in the afternoon
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that in the morning, when the כיור is full, the כהן washes from the upper spouts. In the afternoon, when the water is low, he washes from the lower spouts.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: in the morning, when the כיור is full, he washes his hands and feet from the upper spout. In the afternoon, when the water has gone down, he washes his hands and feet from the lower spout.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא explains that the spouts were placed at two heights, to match the water level during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Over the day, washing lowers the water in the כיור. Spouts at the top serve the full morning level, and spouts at the bottom still work once the water is low.

phrases.english: It was taught: in the morning, when it is full —
he sanctifies his hands and feet from the upper one,
in the afternoon, when it is low —
he sanctifies his hands and feet from the lower one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail about the spouts from Step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spouts were at two heights: the upper ones for the full morning level and the lower ones for the low afternoon level.

steps.title: משנה: בן קטין also made a מוכני for the כיור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: בן קטין also built a מוכני (a device) for the כיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also made a מוכני for the כיור, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה. This sets up a question about what the word מוכני means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water left in the כיור overnight becomes פסול. The משנה says בן קטין made a device to solve this problem, but it does not say what the device looked like.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He too.' Adds another of בן קטין's improvements.

phrases.english: He also made a machine
for the basin, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next improvement by בן קטין in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן קטין made a מוכני for the כיור.

steps.title: What is a מוכני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word מוכני means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a מוכני?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple word-meaning question about the משנה. It is setting up אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a question about a word, not a challenge to the משנה. The גמרא only wants to identify the device.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is?' A standard question asking for a definition.

phrases.english: What is a machine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the term quoted in Step 36.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the device called מוכני was.

steps.title: אביי: a wheel that lowered the כיור
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the מוכני was a wheel used to lower the כיור into a pit of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it was a wheel that lowered it down.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question: the מוכני was a wheel system for sinking the כיור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night the wheel lowered the כיור into a pool or pit, so its water stayed joined to the larger body of water. That kept the water from becoming פסול through being left overnight (לינה), so the water was still usable in the morning.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the משנה here.

steps.whatToRemember: בן קטין's two improvements to the כיור: twelve spouts so twelve כהנים could wash at once, and a wheel (מוכני) to sink the כיור so its water would not become פסול overnight.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A wheel that would sink it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מוכני was a wheel that lowered the כיור.

steps.title: מונבז המלך made golden handles for the vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: מונבז המלך made the handles of all the כלים used on יום הכפורים out of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: מונבז המלך made all the handles of the vessels (out of gold), etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה about another donor to the מקדש. This sets up the question that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After discussing בן קטין's spouts and מוכני for the כיור, the משנה lists another person remembered for good: מונבז המלך. He paid to make the handles of the יום הכפורים כלים out of gold. The word וכו׳ tells us the quote is shortened, and the rest of the משנה line continues.

keyTerms.meaning: King Munbaz, a king who converted to Judaism and gave generously to the מקדש
Vessels, the utensils used in the עבודה
'Etc.', meaning the quote continues past this point

phrases.english: King Munbaz
phrases.notes: A convert king of Adiabene, praised for his generosity.

phrases.english: made all the handles of the vessels, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה means the handles of the יום הכפורים כלים, made of gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹנְבַּז הַמֶּלֶךְ עָשָׂה כָּל יְדוֹת הַכֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's line about בן קטין (steps 36-38) to the next line about מונבז המלך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מונבז המלך donated golden handles for all the כלים used on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Why not make the vessels themselves of gold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if מונבז wanted to beautify the מקדש, he should have made the whole כלים of gold, not just the handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him make the vessels themselves of gold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a pointed question about מונבז's gift: why only gold handles? This sets up an answer that will explain his choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that a rich king who wants to honor the מקדש would do the most generous thing, which is making entire golden כלים. Doing only the handles looks like a strange half-measure. So the גמרא demands an explanation for why he limited his gift.

keyTerms.meaning: Them themselves (the actual vessels, not just a part)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about the meaning of the words. The words are clear. The גמרא is challenging the logic of the gift: why not give more?

phrases.english: Let him make the vessels themselves of gold!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pushing back here: why not make the whole thing gold? The answer comes on the next amud (37b).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic of the gift described in the משנה line quoted in step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's report that מונבז made only the handles of gold.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A donor who wanted to honor the מקדש with gold would naturally make the entire כלים of gold, so limiting the gift to handles needs an explanation.
